title: The refund that paid twice
blurb: A retry generated a new PSP idempotency key.
prompt: A customer received two refunds for one return, because the draft generated a fresh idempotency key per PSP attempt and retried after a timeout. The same ledger let two partial refunds pass the same remaining balance. Review it, fix it, and prove retries share a key and the lifetime cap holds.
aiNote: The draft creates a new idempotency key for every PSP retry, so the provider sees two independent refunds, and its ledger check-then-add is non-atomic, so two concurrent partial refunds both pass against one remaining balance.
testIdea: Time out the PSP call and assert the retry carries the same key and the provider records one refund; race two partial refunds that together exceed the balance and assert one is refused; reconcile the read endpoint against PSP records after a crash.
followUps: When should a refund be manual instead of automatic?
How would you handle a PSP that does not support idempotency keys?
What does the customer see while a refund is pending reconciliation?
